To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a sensitive and specific method for measuring 5-Hmd C, 5-F odC, 5-H mdU and 5-Ca dC in genomic DNA of mammalian cells and tissues.

the LC-MS/MS method developed here can quantitate 5-Hmd, 5-Fo and 5-Ca derivatives of 5-mdC and 5-hydroxy-methyl deamination product 5-Hmd in DNA with high sensitivity and specificity, and that 5-Fod and 5-Cod are present in mammalian DNA in much lower amounts than previously thought.

we have developed a robust and sensitive method for measuring 5-hydroxy-5-methylcytidine (5-Hmd C), 5-formyl-5-methyldeoxycytidin (5-FodC) and 5-carbonyl-5-methyl deoxycytid (5-CadC) in genomic DNA of human cultured cells and multiple mammal tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analytical methodology to accurately measure the 5-mdC oxidation products in cellular and tissue DNAs.
the quantitative assessment of Tet-induced 5-mdC oxidation products in cellular and tissue genomic DNA.
the accurate measurements of 4 types of 5-mdC oxidation products in genomic DNA of mammalian cells and tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Tet family dioxygenases oxidize 5-mdC in DNA to yield 5-Hmd, 5-Fo, and 5-Ca derivatives, and that the levels of 2’ deoxycytidine derivatives are much higher than those of 2’deoxyuridine derivatives.
the levels of 1) 5-HmdD, 2) 5-FodD and 3) 5-CadD are significantly higher in the brain than the skin, and 4) the levels of 4) 5-FdU and 5) 5-CdU are significantly lower in the brain than in the skin.
5-HmdCs are the most abundant oxidized derivatives of 5-mdC in mammalian DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5-HmdCs are the major oxidation products of 4-methylcytosines in mammalian DNA.
Tet-mediated 5-mdC oxidation products are abundant and widespread in mammalian cells and tissues, but the levels of 2’deoxyuridine derivatives are low.
we have developed a quantitative method to measure 5-Hmd, 5-Fo, 5-CA and 5-HU in DNA and have shown that these 5-md derivatives exist at different levels in different cells, tissues and organs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5-HmdCs are the most abundant Tet-induced oxidation products, which may be the most relevant to the active DNA demethylation process in mammals.

the 5-hydromethylcytosine (5-Hmd) derivatives of cytosine in DNA are present at a very high abundance in mammalian genomes and tissues, and their accurate quantification in DNA will be critical for understanding the role(s) of 5-HmCs in epigenetic gene regulation and in human diseases.

the LC-MS/MS method can be used to measure 5-Hmd, 5-Fo, 5-Ca and 5-Hm derivatives of mdC in DNA with high sensitivity and accuracy, and the levels of 2’ deoxynucleosides containing 5-Hm in DNA are much higher than previously reported.
